analysisRule.R1: Units inside the kernel: metres, kilograms, seconds, radians, m/s. A caller who holds arcseconds, pixels or km/s converts with ARCSEC, an explicit pixel scale in radians per pixel, or 1000. There is no default pixel scale, cosmology or velocity dispersion.
analysisRule.R2: The mass inside the Einstein radius is M(<theta_E) = pi Sigma_cr (theta_E D_l)^2 with Sigma_cr = c^2 D_s / (4 pi G D_l D_ls). It is the mass inside the circle in which the mean convergence is one, exact for an axially symmetric lens, for a singular isothermal sphere equal to pi sigma^2 theta_E D_l / G, and unchanged by the mass-sheet transformation (which preserves the critical curves). It is the total projected mass in the circle, dark and luminous, and says nothing about the profile inside it.
analysisRule.R3: The singular isothermal sphere's Einstein angle is theta_E = 4 pi (sigma / c)^2 D_ls / D_s with sigma the one-dimensional velocity dispersion of the lens's mass; a stellar dispersion measured from a spectrum is not that number and no factor between them is assumed or tested here (E3 is NOT RUN).
analysisRule.R4: The arc-radius measurement is the geometric least-squares circle through the marked points, found by Gauss-Newton from the algebraic start with the covariance (J^T W J)^-1, the per-coordinate position sigma declared by the caller (refused with 'no-sigma' when absent). The centre is fixed (the radius is the weighted mean distance, its variance 1/sum(w) plus the first-order term from the centre's declared covariance) or free. A free-centre fit with fewer than five points, or with sigma_r / r above 0.25, is 'not-constrained' with its code; a fixed-centre fit with fewer than two points is refused.
analysisRule.R5: The statistical interval of the mass at a two-sided level L is [M(theta_E - z sigma), M(theta_E + z sigma)] with z the normal quantile of (1 + L) / 2, from the statistical sigma of the radius; it is asymmetric because M goes as theta_E squared; a lower end of theta_E is clipped at zero. Redshifts carry no uncertainty and the cosmology is the caller's; a list of alternative cosmologies, when supplied, is reported as a separate model-limited spread and never folded into the statistical interval.
analysisRule.R6: A single arc is the image of a source that need not lie on the axis: for the singular isothermal sphere the outer image sits at theta_E (1 + y), so the radius is an upper bound of theta_E. With the caller's sourceOffsetMax y_max (in Einstein radii) theta_E lies in [r / (1 + y_max), r]; the mass bracket is that range widened by two statistical sigma at each end and the narrow statistical interval is NOT offered as the mass. Without a y_max the bracket uses y_max = 1 (theta_E in [r/2, r], the mass in [M(r)/4, M(r)]) and the interval is null.
analysisRule.R7: An arc without a lens redshift (missing, not finite, or not positive), or without a source redshift, returns status 'not-constrained' with the code 'no-lens-redshift' or 'no-source-redshift', the angular Einstein radius with its sigma in radians, and a null mass. No redshift is assumed or defaulted.
analysisRule.R8: A lens whose source redshift is not greater than the lens redshift, a non-flat cosmology (|Om + OL - 1| above 1e-9), a non-positive H0 and a negative density are refused with a code; the distance kernel is flat only (D_ls is the difference of comoving distances over 1 + z_s).
analysisRule.R9: The image inversions need one image on each side of the lens: the singular isothermal sphere gives theta_E = (theta_+ + |theta_-|) / 2 and beta = (theta_+ - |theta_-|) / 2; the point lens gives theta_E = sqrt(theta_+ |theta_-|); two positions of the same sign are refused 'images-same-side', one image is 'not-constrained' 'single-image'. The kernel names the model it assumed and returns the other model's value beside it (modelDisagreement); a pair cannot tell the models apart.
analysisRule.R10: A leg judged against the oracle uses the oracle's file of results written before the kernel was run on those inputs; a leg for which the oracle or a file is absent is NOT RUN.

verdictFunction.what: the Part A kernel verdict, a function of the rows alone: A when every closed-form leg (A1 to A7), every oracle leg that was run (B1 to B5) and every refusal leg (D1 to D5) passes and C1, C2 and C3 pass; B when A1 to A7, B1 to B5 and D1, D2, D4 and D5 pass but a coverage leg (C1, C2, C3) or D3 fails: the enclosed mass and its closed forms are claimable and the interval's coverage is not; C when any of A1 to A7, B1 to B5, D1, D2, D4 or D5 fails: nothing of the kernel is claimable. The product verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED while B6, E1 and E2 are NOT RUN. The consumers clause (a viewer mode, a lesson, a pack) is unmet whatever the kernel verdict.

amendments.what: The ensemble draws the Einstein angle directly, log-uniform in [3, 30] arcsec (a radius of 30 to 300 pixels at 0.1 arcsec per pixel); the singular-isothermal-sphere dispersion is then derived from it through R3 and reported in the truth manifest instead of being drawn log-uniform in [150, 1000] km/s. The redshifts (z_l uniform in [0.1, 0.6], z_s = z_l + uniform [0.5, 2]), the pixel scale, the noise (1 pixel per coordinate) and every coverage band are unchanged.
amendments.why: Recorded before any validator run, by arithmetic and before the kernel had produced a number: at (z_l, z_s) near (0.35, 1.35) D_ls / D_s is about one half, and a dispersion of 150 km/s then gives theta_E of about 0.3 arcsec, 3 pixels, so a radius with a 1 pixel noise per coordinate could never be constrained and C1's 'no world is refused' would test the world draw, not the kernel (the contract's sentence for the worlds says theta_E 3 to 30 arcsec was the intended range). No bound moved.
